artifacts.summary: Confirms the missing/empty file_scope visibility gap in validate-state.sh and orchestrate-predispatch-review.sh, clarifies that glob-shaped entries are invisible only to the Overlap predicate (not to the already-working Containment consumer), recommends new Check 10/11 and Class F/G (not reusing the addendum's 'Class C', which collides with the existing self-modification class), flags the validate-artifact.sh --strict/promotion-criterion precedent as reusable but notes validate-state.sh has no --strict flag yet, and shows the dispatch's cited historical counts (37/38, 27/49/22/17/5) no longer reproduce against either repo's live, continuously-orchestrated state.json.

memory_candidates.content: In this codebase, the bash glob-metacharacter test `case "$x" in *[*?\[]*) ... ;; esac` (or its jq equivalent `test("[*?\\[]")`) already exists in path_covered_by_scope() (lib/file-scope-overlap.sh) and _sibling_territory_classify_entry() (orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh). Before adding a new glob-detection check, reuse/centralize this idiom (e.g. as a shared jq def in FILE_SCOPE_OVERLAP_JQ_DEFS) rather than transcribing a third/fourth independent copy.

file-footprint-overlap.md defines two distinct file_scope predicates: the symmetric Overlap Rule (deliberately glob-free per its own Non-Goals section, used by validate-state.sh Check 8 and predispatch-review Class C/D/E) and the one-directional Containment predicate (path_covered_by_scope(), which DOES match glob-shaped entries, used by git-snapshot.sh). A glob-shaped file_scope entry is only invisible to Overlap-based collision/coarseness checks, not to Containment consumers -- word any new WARN as 'invisible to overlap detection', never as 'invalid syntax'.

Historical file_scope coverage counts cited in a task description (e.g. 'N/M active tasks have file_scope') are snapshots of a live, continuously-orchestrated specs/state.json and drift within days -- do not hardcode them as test assertions or literal acceptance-criteria targets. Reproduce the check LOGIC against a small hand-crafted fixture (this repo's existing convention: test-validate-state.sh's Check 8/9 fixtures), and treat any run against a live state.json as an informational measurement only.

user_decision.note: Two judgment calls were made and recorded in the report's Decisions section (new Class F/G instead of reusing the addendum's 'Class C', and glob entries are surfaced as invisible-to-overlap rather than rejected as invalid) -- these are ordinary planning-level calls the plan phase can adopt or override with the full rationale in hand; neither requires the user's own judgment before planning can proceed.
